facts.text: I've been having episodes of dizziness.
The episodes come on suddenly.
I get a false feeling of motion, and occasionally a spinning sensation.

facts.item: symptoms triggered by change in position
facts.text: The dizziness and the spinning depend on my position.
I haven't had any headaches.
I don't have any ringing in my ears.
Apart from my age-related hearing loss, my hearing hasn't changed.
I haven't felt nauseated.
I haven't vomited.
I haven't had any respiratory infections recently.
I haven't been ill recently.
Apart from my hearing, there haven't been any significant changes in my health.
I haven't had any injuries recently.
I have age-related hearing loss.
Apart from my hearing, I don't have any significant medical history.
I haven't had any significant surgery.
I've never been told I had Meniere's disease.
I've never had vestibular neuritis.
I've never had labyrinthitis.
I'm a retired school teacher.
I live alone.
I don't smoke.
I have a glass of wine occasionally.
I enjoy light gardening.

findings.name: gait
findings.result: Steady; no signs of imbalance when not experiencing vertigo.

findings.name: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
findings.result: Positive: right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine.

findings.name: audiometry
findings.result: Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, consistent with presbycusis. No sudden drops in hearing indicative of Meniere's disease or labyrinthitis.

findings.name: videonystagmography
findings.result: Normal vestibular response except for the response elicited during the Dix-Hallpike maneuver, consistent with BPPV.

findings.name: brain MRI
findings.result: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts that would suggest a central cause of vertigo.

quotes.f003: a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning
quotes.f012: significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss

f007: The ROS 'denies ... hearing loss' contradicts the known presbycusis; read with p004 ('No hearing loss besides presbycusis') as no new hearing loss.
f015: 'No significant past medical ... history' is read as apart from the presbycusis stated in the History.

x007.source_text: Steady, no signs of imbalance when not experiencing vertigo

x008.source_text: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV

x009.source_text: Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, consistent with presbycusis. No sudden drops in hearing indicative of Meniere’s disease or labyrinthitis.

x010.source_text: Normal vestibular response with the exception of response elicited during Dix-Hallpike maneuver, consistent with BPPV.

x011.source_text: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts that would suggest central causes of vertigo.

x008: Horizontal nystagmus on Dix-Hallpike is atypical: posterior-canal BPPV gives torsional, upbeating nystagmus; horizontal-canal BPPV is usually shown by the supine roll test. Kept as given.

Source interpretation removed from the result (source: 'Positive: right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine, suggestive of BPPV.'); a bedside examination returns the finding, not the diagnosis.

leakage.reason: The videonystagmography result says 'consistent with BPPV' (pool flag: test_results); kept as the test's answer.

source_issues: Diagnosis abbreviations appear in visible results (Dix-Hallpike 'suggestive of BPPV', VNG 'consistent with BPPV'); flagged by the source pool as requiring cleanup.
The ROS denies hearing loss although the History and p004 record presbycusis.
Horizontal nystagmus on the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre is atypical for the canal it tests.
notes: Patient texts and items avoid the gold words ('vertigo', 'positional', 'benign', 'paroxysmal'): the patient describes dizziness, a false feeling of motion and spinning, and position dependence. 'vertigo' is only a controller-facing alias of f003.
Position dependence applies to both the dizziness and the spinning, so it is a standalone fact (f004).
Presbycusis is a known diagnosis the patient can name (f014); the denials of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis are prior-diagnosis denials (medical_history).
Gold label kept as the source gives it (with '(BPPV)'), only re-capitalised.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with episodes of dizziness and vertigo.
